summary: Backend-only verification of iter82 trainee vibrancy parity + Discover Trainees. Re-ran the 10 in-tree iter82 tests (all pass) and added a 15-case regression+edge suite covering trainer-side endpoints, discover-item shape, ObjectId leak guard, accent-color whitelist variants, bad-base64 handling, and unauthenticated PUT. Result: 23 passed, 1 xfailed (known parity gap), 1 real failure exposing a 500 on bad base64 input. Spec requirements (1)-(11) are all met functionally; two RCAs flagged below.

minor.issue: Returns 500 Internal Server Error when 'data' is not valid base64. binascii.Error from base64.b64decode is uncaught at routes/profile_routes.py:814. Should return 400 with a descriptive message. Affects BOTH trainee and trainer (shared code path).

Empty string accentColor='' is accepted with 200 and stored as ''. Likely intended as a 'clear' affordance, but the trainee endpoint should either DELETE-style clear it (set to null) or reject empty strings. Trainer endpoint behaves the same.

Response does NOT include 'highlights' key, but GET /api/trainee-profiles/{id} does. Parity gap. Either expose highlights inline on the trainer GET (matching trainee) or document that highlights must always be fetched via /highlights subresource.

action_items: Wrap base64.b64decode in profile_routes.py:upload_highlight_base64 (line 814) with try/except binascii.Error -> raise HTTPException(400, 'Invalid base64 payload'). Same fix applies to the trainer variant.
Decide policy on empty accentColor: either persist as null or reject with 400. Apply consistently to trainer + trainee endpoints.
Add 'highlights' to TrainerProfileResponse (or strip it from TraineeProfileResponse) to make the two profile GETs consistent.

(Nit) The TraineeProfile/TrainerProfile accent-color endpoints use a whitelist palette, but the iter82 description in the request says 'rejects invalid colors / accepts valid hex like #6C5CE7'. Update the human-facing docs to clarify the whitelist (currently 10 colors).
critical_code_review_comments: profile_routes.py:upload_highlight_base64 — missing try/except around base64.b64decode causes 500s on malformed user input. Standard HTTP hygiene gap.
TrainerProfileResponse vs TraineeProfileResponse drift: trainee includes 'highlights' inline, trainer does not. Pick one; the iter82 spec implies parity.
Discover endpoint correctly excludes the caller, requires auth (403 without token), excludes Mongo _id, and joins users for fullName. No ObjectId leakage observed.
Cross-user 403 enforcement verified on vibe and highlights endpoints — good.

seed_data_creation: Tests seed bio/vibe/accent on the iter25 trainee to ensure they appear in the discover feed. Highlights are uploaded then immediately deleted in lifecycle tests to leave no residue.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Spec items (1)-(11) all functionally pass against the live preview backend. The new regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_iteration82_regression_and_edges.py covers trainer-side endpoints, discover shape, and edge cases. The single failing test (test_trainee_highlight_bad_base64) demonstrates the 500 bug — re-run it after main agent fixes the base64 try/except in profile_routes.py:upload_highlight_base64 to confirm. The xfail on test_trainer_profile_response_keys will turn green automatically once 'highlights' is added to TrainerProfileResponse.
rca of the issue: RCA #1 (500 on bad base64): /app/backend/routes/profile_routes.py line 814 calls base64.b64decode(data_b64) directly. Python's binascii.Error propagates up to FastAPI which returns 500. Reproduction: POST /api/trainee-profiles/{id}/highlights/base64 with data='!!!not-base64!!!'. Fix: try: content = base64.b64decode(data_b64, validate=True) except (binascii.Error, ValueError): raise HTTPException(400, 'Invalid base64 data'). RCA #2 (highlights missing on trainer GET): TrainerProfileResponse in models.py does not declare a 'highlights' field, while TraineeProfileResponse does. Add `highlights: List[Dict] = []` to TrainerProfileResponse and populate it in the assembler (mirroring the trainee path) for parity.
